svg.text: Automated Crack Detection in TXM Images
Full workflow: pixel-level detection → manual correction → fully automated retrain & deploy, worked example: 338_13

text.tspan: of raw min/max, robust to outlier

svg.text: Unlike a manual review-and-approve loop, (F) deploys itself -- gated by 5 objective checks, not a human judgment call

text.tspan: Browser paint tool: add missed crack,
only if all pass, otherwise leaves

svg.text: deployed model auto-refreshes the paint tool AND powers stage (C) on the next image

text.tspan: Figure 1. Automated crack-detection pipeline for transmission X-ray microscopy (TXM) images. A raw float32 tile is percentile-normalized (A) and
described by 17 multi-scale features per pixel -- intensity-trend, gradient, Laplacian, and texture at radii from 2 to 64px (B) -- which an MLP
neural network classifier (chosen over RandomForest/ExtraTrees/HistGradientBoosting by benchmarked accuracy on the real production training recipe,
see benchmark_figures/) converts into a per-pixel crack probability (C). Post-processing (D) applies hysteresis thresholding restricted to grow only
from already-shape-validated regions (never spontaneously creating a new one), fills small interior holes, rejects ring/dust artifacts by topology
and eccentricity, and blanks a border margin, producing the final mask, overlay, and stats. A human can then review that output in a browser paint
tool -- add missed crack, erase false positives, or click-to-remove a whole false-positive region at once (E) -- and those corrections combine with
the original Ilastik-derived bootstrap labels to retrain the classifier. Unlike a manual review-and-approve loop, the retrained candidate is
deployed automatically, gated by 5 objective checks that each guard a regression this project actually hit during development: accuracy against
corrected ground truth, border/edge density spikes, spontaneous new-artifact area, degenerate output, and whether corrected pixels actually changed
(F). A verified model deploys itself with no human sign-off, and the paint tool detects the swapped file and refreshes its own cached predictions
